key_facts: On Sept. 22, 2023, Swift driver recruiters Robin Kaufman and Matt Hutto emailed Plaintiff through Tenstreet about completing a driver application. On Sept. 25, Tenstreet posted a DriverIQ employment document and an FMCSA Clearinghouse result; FMCSA emailed that SWIFT TRANSPORTATION CO OF ARIZONA LLC (USDOT 54283) had requested Clearinghouse access. On Sept. 26, Swift Recruiting emailed an encrypted pre-adverse letter. On Oct. 5, Swift sent a post-adverse letter stating it had decided not to employ Plaintiff based in whole or in part on consumer reports from Asurint, Tenstreet, DriverIQ, FMCSA-DOT, and Equifax Work Number. The decrypted pre-adverse packet is a Lerma file, not a UPS file: National Criminal without Sex Offender Clear / No Reportable Records Found; federal criminal Clear; San Joaquin / Santa Clara / Washoe / Clark county criminal Clear; NSOPW still Processing on every snapshot, never completed, no hit, no California-registry source; Clearinghouse Driver Not Prohibited, no open violations. What the packet does contain — Class A CDL, an April 22, 2022 improper-lane MVR, PSP inspections, CDLIS license-identity match — is not information disclosed pursuant to Penal Code § 290.46. Do not treat this packet as proof that Home Depot or Best Buy used the registry; it proves the opposite pattern at a different employer.
procedural_status: Complaint retired. Do not execute on September 8, 2026. Do not file before the September 26 / October 5, 2026 outer bounds. The decrypted pre-adverse packet refutes a California-registry source and would support a Lerma dismissal if the § 290.46(j) count were filed. No CRD charge. No demand. The review-draft PDF remains in the file only as the abandoned pleading.

risk: Filing the current § 290.46(j) count on this paper is the Lerma dismissal: the report is in hand and shows ordinary court/MVR/PSP records plus an incomplete NSOPW with no California-registry source. Keep Swift off the September 8 desk. Do not use this packet to name a Home Depot or Best Buy vendor.
